candidate.summary: Shiny for Python has path traversal in bookmark restore

verified.exploit_entry_point: An HTTP GET to the application root (the real browser entry point) carrying a client-chosen bookmark id in the query string (?_state_id_=...). With server-side bookmarking enabled, the root request restores saved state for that id: the id is joined to the store path (cwd/shiny_bookmarks/<id>) with no validation, and input.json/values.json are read from the resulting directory. Because the id is used unvalidated, it can be a relative or absolute path that resolves OUTSIDE the store, so the server reads an attacker-named directory. Restored input values are rendered into the returned HTML, which is how the test observes that an out-of-store file was read (a planted sentinel marker appears in the page). Driven in-process via starlette.testclient.TestClient (no network).
variants: Relative '../OUTSIDE' -> cwd/OUTSIDE (sibling of the store): reads planted input.json, sentinel leaks into HTML on vuln; blocked after fix.
Percent-encoded '%2e%2e%2fOUTSIDE' -> decodes to '../OUTSIDE' once the query string is parsed (exercises the decode-then-use ordering).
Nested 'legit123/../../OUTSIDE' -> climbs out from under a plausible leading segment to cwd/OUTSIDE.
Absolute path (a tmp dir outside the project) supplied as the id -> pathlib join discards the store prefix entirely; contains NO '..', so it defeats a dotdot-only block.
Absolute path to a second out-of-store location -> same class, different target.
code_paths: RestoreContext.from_query_string -> _load_state_qs (server-store branch) -> local_restore_dir -> _local_dir(id) builds cwd/shiny_bookmarks/<id> and reads input.json/values.json
the restored input set is consumed by restore_input() during UI render on GET /, so the read value is reflected into the response HTML
verified.project_tests_run: The repo has no dedicated bookmark-restore tests at the vulnerable parent commit (the upstream security tests were ADDED by the fix commit and are excluded). tests/pytest/test_destroy.py exercises adjacent bookmark machinery (proxy registration/cleanup) and passes at the vulnerable commit on CPython 3.11 (75 passed). The verifier does not run /app's own tests (untrusted); it runs independent copies under /tests. Confirmed with pytest from source on CPython 3.11: at the vulnerable commit all 6 security tests FAIL (traversal succeeds) and all 6 functional tests PASS; after the upstream source fix all 12 PASS.

notes: Pure Python, no services. python:3.11-slim base. shiny installed editable from the vulnerable commit (NOT PyPI, which ships the fixed 1.6.4). Verifier runs in shared mode. The exploit is observed end-to-end over HTTP: a restored input value is rendered into the page, so a planted out-of-store sentinel marker shows up in the response when traversal succeeds.
